key_insight: This paper moves cross-view object geo-localization beyond simple 2D appearance matching by making geometry a first-class signal. It also pairs the model with a large, high-fidelity building dataset to better support real-world localization.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of locating an object across different views, such as ground or drone images matched to satellite imagery, where existing methods struggle because they depend too much on 2D visual similarity and lack rich geometric supervision, diverse prompts, and standard field-of-view data.
method: Introduces a large-scale building dataset with over 220,000 geo-tagged samples and high-fidelity geometric information.
Proposes a unified single-stage framework for cross-view object geo-localization that incorporates geometry-aware reasoning.
Targets more robust matching across view changes by using both appearance cues and spatial/geometric structure.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a more realistic path to object localization in cross-view settings by improving robustness to viewpoint shifts. The dataset and unified framework can also serve as a stronger benchmark for future research in geospatial vision and remote sensing.
visual_elements: A three-panel pipeline diagram showing query view, geometry-aware matching, and satellite localization output.

paper_title: Beyond 2D Matching: A Unified Single-Stage Framework for Geometry-Aware Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
paper_authors: Liyao Wang, Ruipu Wu, Haojun Xu, Lei Shi, Linjiang Huang
